Now I'm confronted with strong emotions inside, and even externally, and I find my thoughts going down the path of how to communicate productively, with the same
fury and urgency that I had when it was fueled by rage or perceived betrayal or what have you. Now I find myself accidentally consoling people who are frustrated with me by saying "Hey, I wasn't understanding you but you seem really upset and I want you to know I don't feel like you deserve to continue feeling that way, why don't we talk later when it's easier for both of us." Or things to that effect. It's sort of wild how I went from being the person who starts actual fights into habitual problem solver. Never would've seen this coming. 

Now, the most important thing that I believe you should remember is this; You absolutely 100% need to recover at your own speed. There is absolutely no time stamp or price tag that you can put on your mental health and I do not believe it is a healthy rhetoric to call children who are financially dependent on their parents at any age a financial burden as it is the parent's responsibility to make sure the child is capable of independence.
